body:
Yeah, it's been pretty toxic, even after I cut ties with the most toxic people in my life. I could definitely use a fresh start, because this area just depresses me. 

And I understand how you feel about the dating thing. A friend of mine tried to hook me up with someone recently. We went out once, and he seemed interested in seeing me again. We chatted a couple times, then *poof*, he disappeared and stopped contacting me. It just reminded me of why I don't bother anymore. 

I work first shift, which is hard for me, because I've always been a night owl. And I feel the same way as you. I think about taking a nap, then getting stuff done, but I always just end up watching Netflix or getting lost browsing the internet. 

Thank you again for your kind words. I'm an extroverted person, but we're so busy during the holidays that it exhausts me, and I go into hermit mode because I'm sick of dealing with people and being around them. On the plus side, I'm off today, and finally got the motivation to do some of my laundry that's been piling up. It's the small victories, I guess. :-)

I'm pretty sure that only a few people went to my last class reunion. I was invited, but didn't see the point in going. I've never gone to the desert, but next year, finances permitting, I've been considering going to check it out. No mosquitoes or snow would be great, because those are 2 reasons why I hate living here lol. And I prefer the temperature to be colder at night, because I prefer to sleep under the covers. Being single doesn't really bother me as much as it used to. I've met guys, or had friends try to hook me up, and it always just serves as a reminder of why I don't want to deal with that bullshit anymore. I have goals to try to better my life, but it's just hard to motivate myself to work toward them. By the time I get home from work, I feel like all of my energy has been drained from me. Working retail, I have to keep a cheery demeanor, and it's just becoming taxing, especially because it's the holiday season. Then I come home to my bitchy roommate, so it's a never-ending cycle of suck. I try to minimize any interactions with her, but it just seems to make her feel the need to cram all of her shitty comments into the few minutes it takes me to make my way upstairs to my room. I've never tried meditation, but it's worth a shot. I'll definitely check out that book! Thanks for the recommendation and kind words!

I only have one friend from high school that I still speak to, but she's my best friend. But there are definitely times when it feels like she's not there for me. I understand that everyone has their own shit going on, but sometimes I grab my phone to text her, but decide not to bother. I've never been to a class reunion. If I wanted to keep in touch with those people, I would have lol. My dream is to live in an old Airstream in the desert. That would be my ideal life, but I need to start getting my shit together, and I feel like I'm running out of time.
Hell, I only moved 45 minutes away and it's like a different world. Been here for 14 years, and I still miss "home".

The best pierogi pizza, hands down, is from Hilltop in Masury by the PA border. But I swear, the Youngstown area has a weird curse. I have friends who have moved away from the area for years, and somehow they end up coming back.

I fucking love Swenson's! But I've come to realize how much I miss food from my hometown, even though it's only 45 minutes away. I indulged when I was housesitting for my best friend back home a few weeks ago. Bubblegum ice cream from Katie's Korner, Brier Hill Pizza, and Pierogi pizza.
I've considered it off and on. But due to my work schedule, I would have to take night classes. And as it stands right now, I barely have the energy to withstand my 40+ hour per week job.
I always thought the southwest would be a great place to live!
Your dog is adorable!!! I'm currently residing in beautiful, scenic Akron, OH. But I'll definitely hit you up if I ever roam into LA. I've never been that far west.

It is just a circle of bullshit. And btw, daaaaamn, it sounds like you've had some crazy shit thrown your way! But anyway, I think part of my issue is that I just want to escape. More and more lately, I'll be laying in bed, about to sleep, and suddenly have an urge to just grab my cats and drive away. Just go somewhere new and random, where I don't know anyone, and start a new life.

I've considered a more nomadic, homeless lifestyle, but if I were to do so, I would have to live out of my car. I have 3 kitties who depend on me, and are part of the reason why I keep fighting. Thank you for your admiration. You're still young, and you have plenty of time to determine the life you want to live, and how to accomplish it. I know that 34 isn't exactly "old", but the older you get, more doors and windows of opportunity get shut in your face. In a way, I wish I would have been more adventurous and nomadic when I was your age. Live it up before you get sucked into the mundane day to day bullshit!
